phases.title: Core data model — attributes, domains, promote/transfer
Field grammar and noise contract — trig, orient, normalized, exact worley
Attribute ergonomics and seeding — string setAttribute, seed story
Cooking and runtime — per-output cook, 3D cells, unbounded levels
WGSL field compiler — codegen for the field-expression grammar
GPU device runtime — evaluator, cook integration, parity suite
Pervasive GPU adoption — all field nodes, chunked dispatch, buffer pooling
Device-resident pipeline core — fused runs, one readback
Uniform constant params — drop the constant column cost (v0.6.1)
Device-resident instance transforms — compose on GPU, own the buffers
Host-planned asset grouping in the resident run

log.message: Phase 31 complete; v0.8.0. examples/02-forest — the demo that motivated the whole cycle — now runs on the device-resident path with assetAttr: 'species' intact, with the toggle and readout vocabulary v0.7's example established. Browser-verified, and it produced the cycle's best determinism evidence: the batch split reads 4,246 pine / 1,666 bush on BOTH paths, and those are the exact counts the manual already recorded from the CPU path back in v0.7 — the device path reproduced the CPU grouping precisely, which is what one shared groupPointsByAsset was supposed to buy, now confirmed end to end rather than argued structurally. 5,912 x 64 = 369.5 KiB matches the readout, device dispatches read 2 (one per asset), matrices uploaded 0 B, and the CPU toggle uploads exactly the 369.5 KiB the device path avoided: same arithmetic, opposite side of the bus. The fused-members readout says 1 and says why — a string setAttribute is not resident-eligible and breaks the chain one node before the spawn — rather than quietly implying deeper fusion. The example keys its draw on item.deviceBatches rather than the requested mode, so a rejected run degrades honestly instead of feeding CPU meshes a storage-attribute material. Docs: spawn-asset-attr removed from all seven live sites (three mentions remain, each explicitly framed as retired history); the grouping order is now a documented contract callers may depend on; stats.dispatches corrected at three mirrors to per (step, asset), with the pool-bucketing understatement recorded; the string-setAttribute chain break documented as the remaining boundary. The docs agent's own verifier caught four over-general claims in its first draft, the sharpest being that 'the run contains only the spawner' is false in general — resident nodes between the break and the spawn still fuse; it is true of the forest specifically. Also fixed a real defect found along the way: src/index.ts exported VERSION = '0.6.1', stale ever since v0.7.0 shipped, because bumping package.json is a separate act from editing that constant and nothing connected the two. Now correct AND pinned by a test that reads package.json, mutation-checked. That is the same unpinned-constant class as phase 29's PLAN_FORMAT. 1024 tests green.

Phase 30 complete and audited (FIX-FIRST, then fixed): N device batches per cell — one buffer per asset — now flow through WorldThreeBinding and the WebGPU adapter. The phase's premise was that the three side needed no production change; that turned out HALF right, and the half that was wrong mattered. The N-batch data path (retain/build/refcount/release) was already batch-plural and identity-keyed, proven structurally and then empirically with 16 tests driving N=3-5 against unchanged code. But teardown was not: disposeEntry aborted at the first throwing adapter.release, abandoning the other N-1 objects, and dispose() did the same a level up, abandoning whole cells and LEAKING device buffers (reproduced: 2 of 3 handles leaked). The independent audit then found the identical defect class in a third and higher-frequency place: cellReady's unguarded removeCell, where a throwing release of the OUTGOING cell escapes before cells.set, so the INCOMING cell's already-retained handles become unreachable forever and dispose() cannot free them (reproduced: 2 handles / 512 bytes). Plus the CPU-mesh/debug-point dispose loops outside the guard, and a rethrow that masked the original build error with the cleanup error. Three sightings of one defect class argued for one mechanism rather than three catches: a shared `attempt(failure, step)` that runs a teardown step to completion, captures the first failure and carries it forward, used at four sites. It states the invariant once — a throwing teardown must never abort the ownership bookkeeping beside it. Bounds now thread assetId (the cell sphere was exact before phase 29 and became lossy only because of it; two-param callbacks still type-check, and the example compiled untouched). stats.dispatches keeps one per (step, asset), deliberately chunk-invariant. Notable methodological finding: the leak is caught ONLY by the churn test's per-iteration live-set model — every final-state assertion in the suite is blind to it. Browser-verified multi-asset resident rendering here rather than deferring it: a temporary two-asset build of 09-gpu-world drew both geometries from their own device buffers, 2 buffers per cell, 0 B uploaded, bytes exact at cells x 140 x 64, console clean, then reverted. Seam guard byte-identical throughout (HEAD a strict prefix, 140 insertions 0 deletions). 1023 tests green (from 1001).

Phase 29 complete and audited (SHIP): a spawnInstances driven by assetAttr is now a device-resident run terminal, and there is no device-side sort anywhere in the change. The asset key is a host string column by construction, so a new shared groupPointsByAsset (src/spawn/grouping.ts) plans the grouping, the host uploads a permutation, and the compose kernel dispatches once per asset with a base uniform (src = perm[base + i], destination stays i). One output buffer and one detach per asset. buildInstanceBatches consumes the SAME function, so the ordering spec has exactly one implementation and cannot drift — determinism by construction, not by comparison; spawn/instances.test.ts passes unchanged. The 'spawn-asset-attr' opt-out and reason are retired from the source taxonomy, and the two CPU throws became PlanFail rejections so the per-node path raises byte-identical messages. PLAN_FORMAT bumped to /4; APPLY_VERSION/SALT_VERSION deliberately NOT bumped. The independent audit went far past the implementer's own claims: it compared 4,484 kernel variants (the report said 24) and found ZERO differing on wgsl, key, uniform bytes, const slots and bindings; confirmed CPU-spawner output byte-identical over 366 corpus cases on raw f32 bits; traced all five throw/cancel windows and the post-cancellation detach loop as leak-free with 4 buffers out and 4 back across cook/evict/recook; and ran 37 mutations, killing 34. The three survivors were unreachable defensive code plus one genuinely unpinned constant: PLAN_FORMAT could be reverted to /3 with the suite still green. Fixed here with a pin, and the pin was itself mutation-checked (reverting the tag reddens it). One PLAN deviation, verified rather than assumed: 'allow string attributes as u32 slots' was NOT implemented, because under host-planned grouping the key never leaves the host, string attributes are CPU-only in the compiler and setAttribute rejects string mode — the code would be uncallable. PLAN.md corrected rather than left contradicting the source. Doc mirrors of the retired reason remain and belong to phase 31. 1001 tests green (from 955).

v0.8 cycle scheduled (phases 29-31): multi-asset resident spawns, closing v0.7's one documented limitation — assetAttr falls back to CPU, and examples/02-forest spawns with assetAttr so the most representative demo cannot use the device path at all. The feasibility survey INVERTED the recorded stretch, which had assumed a device-side sort/partition. No sort is needed: a resident run always starts from a host Geometry and no resident node can produce a string attribute (setAttribute's resident predicate requires type !== 'string'; run.ts planning throws PlanFail on a string slot), so the asset key is host-resident at plan time BY CONSTRUCTION. The host plans the grouping, uploads a permutation, and the device composes once per asset — no atomics, no prefix sum, no readback, and determinism by construction rather than by matching a GPU sort to CPU semantics. String columns are already Uint32Array table indices, so nothing needs marshalling; only a type check blocks the upload. Second finding that shaped scope: one buffer with per-asset offsets is not viable, because three's bind group emits { binding, resource: { buffer } } with no offset or size (verified in the installed three source and already pinned by our own guard test) — so N buffers, one detach per asset, which is expected to need no three-side production change at all. Scope caveat recorded honestly: the forest's speciesAttr is a string setAttribute and is not resident-eligible, so it breaks the fusable chain and the forest's run will contain exactly ONE member, the spawn. The headline win still lands in full, but docs and demo readouts must not imply deeper fusion. Making string setAttribute resident is the new recorded stretch — and only then would the counting sort actually be required. Every load-bearing claim re-derived against source before scheduling.

Phase 28 complete and audited; v0.7.0. examples/09-gpu-world is now a real example: a streamed world with a live toggle between the device-resident path and a CPU readback path that cooks the same graph, the same fields, on the same device — only the ending differs. Readouts cover live cells, cooked/evicted plus a churn rate, instances drawn, matrices held on device, matrix uploads avoided and matrices uploaded. Browser-verified on a shared device (nvidia/blackwell): the toggle changes the REAL path, not a label — cpuMatrixFloats 0 vs 2240, isStorageAttribute true vs false — and the counters are self-consistent at every sample (259,840 = 29x140x64; 1.0 MiB = 40x420x64). The leak check is the divergence: after a rebuild dropped the world from 92 cells to 12, retained buffers fell 92 to 12 (824 KB to 105 KiB) while the cumulative counter correctly kept its full history at 104. Docs: the resident spawner contract, the shared-device requirement and why it is a platform constraint rather than a convenience, the single-asset limitation with its named fallback reason, the ownership chain, and the pinned three seam, across README/llms.txt/authoring plus a ninth manual chapter and a landing-page card. The audit again earned its cost, and again the most valuable finding was a check that could not fail: probe().backendBufferIsAdopted returned true on the CPU path too (three's own buffer is also >= count*64), so the helper used to verify the device path proved nothing — now null unless the attribute is actually a storage attribute. It also caught the 'readbacks avoided' readout overstating itself: its byte column is count*64, which is the avoided matrix UPLOAD, not the avoided readback (the P/rot/scale columns, 28 B/instance) — renamed to 'matrix uploads avoided', which is both true and exactly symmetric with 'matrices uploaded'. Plus: cell bounding spheres were too small (MAX_INSTANCE_RADIUS 3.2 against a real extent near 8.6, so 21.96 supplied where 26.04 is needed), now derived from named scale constants; a comment claiming binding bytes must equal poolStats bytes, which they cannot (logical count*64 vs pow2 buckets); and a dead toggle after device loss. Separately, a stale doc comment in src/gpu/index.ts told third-party adapter authors to call handle.dispose() — the exact opposite of the enforced contract, and a use-after-free for anyone following it, since one handle can back several aliased cells. 955 tests green.

Phase 27 complete and audited (PASS-with-fixes): instance transforms composed on the GPU now render straight from the device. A WebGPU renderer shares the evaluator's device, and the retained buffer is adopted as a storage instance attribute — the audit's decisive check, which the implementer had not made, is buffer IDENTITY: the buffer three renders from IS the handle's resource. Alongside it: instanceMatrix.array.length is 0, zero matrix-sized Float32Array allocations across a whole cook, no validation errors on a real render, and a staging readback showing 0 of 140 identity matrices — positively excluding the 'everything piles at the origin' failure. Bounds come out-of-band from the cell AABB (no bounds means culling off rather than guessed). Handles are refcounted BY IDENTITY across live cells, which is what makes the parentFor aliasing case safe; verified with a real two-level World in both eviction orders. Steady state stressed to 19,368 cooks / 17,898 evictions — 12.6x the implementer's run — across teleports, boundary reversals, invalidate-in-flight, stationary recooks and radius cycling: retained buffers never exceeded the live cell count and the binding's counter matched the pool's detachedBuffers at every single sample. Two internals are depended on, both isolated and pinned by guard tests. The audit's mutation pass caught 33 of 37 deliberate breakages, fixed three unpinned gaps, and found a vacuous test in the shipped guard suite (an assertion comparing two local constants that could never fail). It also caught its OWN harness reporting a false 24/24 — every run was 'failing' for an unrelated spawn error — by demanding actual failing test names. One real HIGH defect found and fixed: a device item's handles were stranded when an earlier item in the same cell threw, leaking a GPUBuffer per failed cook with nothing else in the library to free it. 955 tests green.

Phase 26 complete and audited (PASS-with-fixes): a fused run ending at spawnInstances composes every 4x4 in WGSL and hands back a retained device buffer with ZERO readback — transforms never touch the CPU. Ownership is three states with a named owner throughout (pool-owned, detached, holder-owned handle), double-dispose is a no-op rather than a double free, and un-disposed handles stay counted in poolStats so a leak is visible instead of silent. Compose parity vs composeTRS: max 4.768e-7 (0.143 f32-ULP), 75.9% bit-identical, translation column and constant slots exactly equal, and a layout witness proves column-major with translation at 12-14 — not transposed. isFusable now admits a resident terminal with one geometry output plus non-geometry pins, refusing everything else across 12 adversarial shapes. Device outputs are never memo-served (volatile entry), proven bounded across 20 distinct-graph cycles. The audit's value was above the run executor, which it confirmed airtight under 24 injected faults: it found FOUR leak paths in cookRun, the worst being a terminal whose instances pin is neither connected nor selected, which composed, detached, and stranded a buffer on every successful cook — silent and monotonic. All four fixed by one mechanism (the cook owns handles until delivery, frees on throw and frees anything undelivered, identity-based so forwarded handles survive) plus five regression tests. It also caught two vacuous test oracles: a measure() that scored NaN as a perfect match, defeating five tolerance assertions, and loops that asserted nothing when empty. Phase 27 inherits a verified 16-site disposal checklist, including that parentFor aliases a parent's outputs into child cells — so disposing on parent evict would be a use-after-free. 904 tests green.

v0.7 cycle started (phases 26-28): GPU-resident World streaming — compose instance transforms on device and hand them to the renderer without a CPU round trip. Feasibility settled first: three 0.185.1 ships three/webgpu and its backend accepts parameters.device, so one GPUDevice can back both the evaluator and a WebGPURenderer (without that the feature is impossible — WebGL cannot read a WebGPU buffer, nor can two devices share one). An architecture survey mapped 19 seams that assume a CPU Float32Array of transforms; two findings shaped scope: spawnInstances is structurally barred from resident runs today (fusion demands exactly one geometry output; it has two), and device-side multi-asset grouping needs a sort/partition over a string-table attribute — the one genuinely GPU-hostile step, so v0.7 fuses the constant-assetId case and falls back for assetAttr. Design fixed: additive and opt-in (WebGL path untouched), buffer lifetime treated as the hard problem rather than the matrix math (explicit pool detach, named owner, eviction ordered against in-flight work, memo cache must not pin device memory), CPU stays the bit-exact reference, and the three backend internal gets version-pinned behind a loud guard test. Also: pcg-ts@0.6.1 published to npm 2026-08-07.

v0.6.1 released. Phase 25 complete and audited (PASS-with-fixes): constant node params inside a resident run now ride the apply kernel's PcgParams uniform (12-byte scalar header padded to a 16-byte boundary, then array<vec4<f32>,4>) instead of materializing a full device column and a dispatch. The demo's five-node chain drops from 156 MB to 120 MB of working set per cook at 1M points (-23.1%) and from 12 member kernels to 9; across the device suites dispatches fall 132 to 99, and the run-too-large boundary moves exactly with the new byte math. Constant VALUES stay out of the generated WGSL — the apply key encodes only which params are constant, their tuple sizes, and their slots — so editing a constant rebinds a uniform and hits the pipeline cache instead of recompiling, which baking literals would have thrashed. Byte-exactness held: the audit built an independent harness reproducing the old column path and found uniform output byte-identical across 16 cases spanning all four apply kinds, plus 16 binding arrangements proving the constants-declare-no-binding remap never mis-wires. One measured exception, confirmed and widened by the audit: D3D12 flushes -0 and the entire subnormal range to +-0 when baked as a WGSL literal but not when loaded from a uniform, so those constants now match the CPU reference where the old column path did not. Bytes therefore can change, so SALT_VERSION bumped gpu1 to gpu2 per its own documented rule (and PLAN's 'bytes never move' wording was corrected rather than left contradicting the code). 853 tests green.

v0.6.0 released. Phase 24 complete: 08-gpu-fields now cooks a five-node fusable chain three ways and times them cold — browser-verified at 500k points as CPU 27.0 s / GPU per-node 1.19 s / GPU fused 443 ms (x66.6 vs CPU, 2.7x vs per-node), with counters reading 1 resident run over 5 fused nodes, 4 readbacks saved, 12 member kernels, zero fallbacks; both GPU hashes reproduce byte-for-byte across reloads, and the 8 MiB cap control forces a visible run-too-large that falls back to per-node. Browser verification caught two real demo defects, both fixed: measuring CPU first could cost the page its WebGPU device (a ~57 s main-thread block trips the browser watchdog) and left the next readback pending forever — GPU paths now measure first and a device-lost handler surfaces the reason instead of hanging; and the counters block, keyed to the last-cooked path, went blank when CPU ran last — it now falls back to the newest GPU report with its source labeled. Headless Node reproduction proved the library itself was never at fault (per-node 635 ms, fused 254 ms at 1M). Docs carry the resident-run contract, the corrected stats.gpu shape, and the honest cost note that constant params still cost a device column and dispatch each. Final gate: 842 tests, clean typecheck, library + examples builds, idempotent docs.

Phase 23 complete and audited (PASS-with-fixes): device-resident runs fuse linear chains of setAttribute/transformPoints/jitterPoints/orientAlongVector into one round trip — attribute columns live in storage buffers across member kernels (in-place, with field temporaries materialized before each apply kernel so a param column can never alias the buffer it writes) and a single readback materializes only written attributes. Verified on hardware: 228 apply-kernel variants compile with zero WGSL diagnostics; 17 chains of 2-8 members execute correctly, 11 of them BIT-EXACT vs CPU on every attribute (incl. mid-run retype, self-read rewrite, 8-member run); float chains 1.33-4.83 rangeUlp against budget 6; a 4.3M-point run fuses in 421 ms byte-identical to CPU; cancellation leaves zero buffers in flight. The audit led with mutation testing — 11 deliberate kernel/planner defects injected one at a time — and the suite as delivered caught 10, the survivor being SSA-epoch rebinding (invisible because the probe's replacement field was the identity), now closed by a new bit-exact chain. The audit also falsified the implementer's zero-bug claim by finding a real contract violation: interior members retained stale per-node cache entries while fused, each pinning an unreachable Geometry — fixed. Implementation note: the first implementation agent was interrupted by credit exhaustion mid-file; the evaluator wiring (shared pipeline cache, getPipeline, planRun/executeRun, maxResidentBytes) was completed by hand. 842 tests green (41 new).

Phase 22 complete and audited (PASS-with-fixes): transformPoints, jitterPoints, orientAlongVector, surfaceSample, and volumeSample now resolve field params on device through a shared resolveOnMaybeGpu helper with gpu:fields provenance — the samplers hand the resolver the exact internal-cloud contexts the CPU path uses, and audit-built adversarial specs (fields reading the very attributes the nodes write) proved CPU and GPU cooks byte-identical in every case. Chunked dispatch (chunkOffset uniform, non-final chunks exact workgroup multiples) retires dispatch-too-large: a 4.3M-element resolve byte-equals CPU in 10 ms; audit re-derived the partition math and fuzzed adversarial chunk overrides. Pow2-bucketed buffer pooling (256 MiB bound, poolStats, dispose) proven observationally invisible across interleaved shapes. Audit fixed two real evaluator defects: NaN dispatch-limit silently produced all-zero uncomputed columns (now rejected at construction), and an OOM-class readback failure returned a still-mapped buffer to the pool, poisoning its bucket (unmap now in finally). 801 tests green (32 new).

v0.6 cycle started (phases 22-24): make the GPU path pervasive (transformPoints/jitterPoints/orientAlongVector/surfaceSample/volumeSample adopt the resolver; chunked dispatch retires dispatch-too-large; pooled buffers), then device-resident pipelines fusing count-preserving field-node chains into single-readback runs under a fixed cache contract (terminal-only caching, boundary splits at external consumers), then demo/docs/v0.6.0. User confirmed the 08-gpu-fields demo renders correctly (visual check that was pending window visibility). npm publish explicitly deferred by user.

v0.5.0 released. Phase 21 complete: example 08-gpu-fields (million-point scatter whose JSON field expressions cook through WGSL compute kernels; CPU/GPU toggle, live CookStats.gpu, per-path FNV hashes, live parity readout) verified interactively in Chrome on the host adapter — 1M GPU cook in ~0.8s with 2 dispatches and zero fallbacks vs ~5s CPU at 100k, GPU hash byte-stable across cold reloads and cold-cache recooks, CPU/GPU hashes distinct as documented, live deviation 5.9 range-ULP within budgets, and toggling paths recooked exactly the field nodes while the scatter source stayed cached (provenance surgery visible in the stats line). One in-browser defect found and fixed: the pre-cook paint wait hung forever in hidden tabs (rAF never fires); now races a timeout. README/llms.txt/authoring document the GPU surface and the measured parity contract; overview site refreshed with the eighth demo; hosted demos rebuilt. Final gate: 769 tests, clean typecheck, library and examples builds. npm publish remains a separate user-driven step.

Phase 20 complete and audited (PASS-with-fixes): GpuFieldEvaluator runs compiled field kernels on a real device behind the core GpuFieldResolver interface — structural device typing (browser and Node bindings both assignable), instance-lifetime pipeline cache, complete fallback vocabulary (no-spec / compile-error / too-many-buffers / dispatch-too-large), CookOptions.gpu threaded through setAttribute, subgraphs, captureAsync, and World. Memo keys gain |gpu:<device salt> exactly when a node would resolve a spec'd field on device, so caches stay provenance-pure across toggles (stats-proven) while the CPU path stays byte-identical. Parity measured on hardware and asserted as budgets: u32/hash/compare families byte-exact across counts and seeds; floats from 1-2 ULP (arith) to the WGSL absolute-error class (asin/acos); four GIGO-class divergences pinned as contract lines. Load-bearing discovery: Dawn destabilizes vitest workers, so all device work runs in plain-Node children (deterministic across 6+ full runs); suites skip visibly without an adapter. Audit re-derived the zero-regression and layering claims, simulated the no-adapter path, and fixed one test-only defect (NaN-blind parity comparator). 769 tests green (41 new).

Phase 19 complete and audited (PASS, zero fixes): compileFieldSpec compiles the complete field-expression grammar to WGSL compute kernels behind the new pcg-ts/gpu subpath — SSA subtree dedup, static broadcast/tuple inference, fused fbm loops, worley exact ring walk, normalized wrapping; the u32 hash library ports bit-exactly (audit re-derived the murmur chains by hand) with all constants imported from the CPU source of truth. getFieldSpec joins fieldToJson as a non-throwing accessor. Audit line-checked six generated kernels as a human WGSL front end: no invalid literals, no layout traps, no identifier collisions. Separately, a Dawn smoke test on the host GPU confirmed the design's core bet empirically: a murmur round dispatched on device is bit-exact vs Math.imul and run-to-run stable, and Dawn's getCompilationInfo can validate every generated kernel in phase 20. 728 tests green (101 new).

v0.5 cycle started: the recorded WebGPU stretch goal scheduled as phases 19-21 (WGSL compiler for the field-expression grammar; opt-in GPU device runtime with cook integration, cache provenance, and a measured parity contract; example + docs + v0.5.0). Design fixed up front from an architecture audit: the serializable field grammar is the GPU surface, pcg-ts/gpu is a guarded subpath, CPU stays the bit-exact reference, u32 hash/random streams port exactly, floats match within documented tolerances. Also committed: example 07-galaxy (streamed spiral galaxy with clickable star systems).

v0.4.0 released. Phase 18 complete: node reference regenerated with category grouping; README/llms.txt/authoring document the mutation and introspection contracts (including disconnect's unknown-pin behavior change); overview site and hosted demos refreshed. Final gate: 627 tests, clean typecheck, idempotent docs.

Phase 17 complete and browser-verified: registry gains optional category metadata (all 25 standard types categorized: source/sampler/point op/filter/attribute/value/spawn/io/composite) and describeSubgraphPins resolves per-instance pins live from the recorded spec, recursing nested wrappers. The graph editor adopted the phase-16 APIs: deletes and disconnects mutate the live mirror instead of rebuilding through JSON. Verified interactively - adding a branch cooks 1 node with everything else cached; deleting it recooks ZERO nodes and the output hash returns to the exact starter value; the palette groups by category. 627 tests green.

Phase 16 complete and audited (PASS): Graph gains removeNode (documented cascade over connections and declared outputs, structural cache eviction, single version bump), hardened disconnect (unknown pins now throw actionably; multi-input survivors keep insertion order), removeOutput, a frozen describe() structure snapshot in insertion order, and frozen getParams copies - with seeds served by the same helper the executor uses. Audit probed mid-cook removals, id reuse, version-bump discipline on every failure path, subgraph ghosts, and World staleness: no defects; one error-message hint improved (removed-node case). 618 tests green.

v0.4 cycle started: editor-grade graph APIs scheduled as phases 16-18 (graph mutation + introspection with exact cache surgery; registry categories + subgraph pin introspection with the editor adopting the new APIs as proof; docs and v0.4.0). Repo is now public (user flipped visibility).

v0.3.0 released. Phase 15 complete: node reference regenerated (transferAttribute's full mapping surface), README/llms.txt/authoring cover the transfer mappings and the graph editor, post-v0.3 backlog recorded (editor-grade graph APIs), VERSION export aligned. Overview site refreshed with the sixth live demo and the v0.3 roadmap; hosted demos rebuilt to include the editor. Final gate: 597 tests, clean typecheck, library and examples builds, idempotent docs.

Phase 14 complete and browser-verified: examples/06-graph-editor, a Svelte 5 node-graph editor built entirely on the public API - registry-driven palette, schema-generated inspector (including field-expression JSON editing), pin connections validated by the live graph with library errors shown verbatim, debounced per-output cooking into the three.js viewport, JSON export/import. Verified interactively: starter graph cooks and renders 350 instances; seed round-trips restore the exact output hash; export-import recooks byte-identically; invalid connections toast the library's message; palette add and node delete recook correctly with the hash returning to the exact starter value. Four public-API gaps recorded for phase 15 (node category metadata, removeNode, structural read API, subgraph pin introspection). 597 tests green; library source untouched.

Phase 13 complete and audited: transferUv (UV-space triangle lookup, barycentric interpolation, seam-correct vertex-domain UVs) and transferRaycast (float64 ray-triangle intersection, DDA grid walk, per-point direction override, maxDistance) join nearest in the transferAttribute node, with deterministic tie rules, exported epsilon policies, and miss-count reporting. Audit fuzzed ~33k queries against an independent brute-force reference and constructed a real sliver-triangle counterexample breaking the cellSize-neutrality invariant - fixed by making the padded-bbox test part of the containment policy on both mappings, restoring grid = brute-force by construction. 597 tests green. Also: live demos now hosted on the Pages site and linked from the overview page.

v0.3 cycle started: stretch tier scheduled as phases 13-15 (uv/raycast attribute transfer; interactive Svelte graph editor built on the registry and serialization; docs and v0.3.0 release). WebGPU compute subgraphs remain recorded, not scheduled. Also since release: public one-page overview site on GitHub Pages (docs/index.html) with theme-token diagrams that survive forced-dark inverters. Phase 13 underway.

v0.2.0 released. Phase 12 complete: node reference regenerated (25 types, idempotent); README, llms.txt, and authoring guide cover the full v0.2 surface; PLAN sketch aligned with the shipped API. Examples simplified with the new nodes and re-verified live in the browser: 03-spline-fence is one graph via orientAlongVector (rendered instances byte-identical), 02-forest selects species declaratively via string setAttribute + assetAttr (71.8/28.2 split on target). Final gate: 562 tests, clean typecheck, library + examples builds.

Phase 11 complete and audited (PASS): per-output cooking — cook(graph, { outputs }) walks only the induced upstream subgraph with exact cache reuse (A-then-B recooks only B's exclusive nodes), sound under cancel/resume with changed selections, surfaced in the World as LevelDef.cookOutputs; opt-in 3D cube cells with the 2D hash chain locked byte-identical, floor-correct negative-coordinate nesting, and documented mixed-mode rules; generationRadius optional on unbounded levels. Audit probed cache staleness, hash collisions (length-prefixed chains, zero found), and boundary metrics — no defects; empty-cookOutputs now rejected at construction and the three.js binding keys all three cell coords. 562 tests green.

Phase 10 complete and audited (clean PASS): setAttribute writes string attributes via the string table (value-list mode with a total floor+clamp selector, or constant mode) with a new serializable stringList param type, making multi-asset spawns fully declarative — spawnInstances already accepted string assetAttr, now pinned by tests. Optional seed param folds through the standard hashCombine chain; setSeed-in-bind documented as sanctioned in the bind contract and authoring guide. geometryDiff now compares string content behind indices. Audit verified bit-compat (old JSON cooks identically, recooks 100% cache-hit) and path-independent seeding under eviction; no defects. 535 tests green.

Phase 9 complete and audited: trig functions (sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/atan2) in field combinators and the JSON grammar; orientAlongVector node whose default +z convention reproduces the spline-fence example's quaternion through the spawner compose path; normalized [0,1] option on all noise fields with machine-readable raw-range metadata (NOISE_RAW_RANGES, noiseOutputRange); exact opt-in worley via ring expansion with a proven r<=3 bound. Audit independently re-derived the range and ring math (all sound) and caught an exact-worley infinite loop on non-finite positions — fixed with a provably-unreachable-for-finite-inputs cap so garbage input degrades like the approximate path. 513 tests green; no goldens moved.

Phase 8 complete and audited: graphs containing subgraph nodes now serialize (recursive versioned payload, cycle-safe both directions, plumbing excluded by recorded id) and deserialize to real code-first subgraph instances that cook byte-identically.
